Catchment-redundancy choropleth map

Source: R/catchment_redundancy_map.R
mysterymaps_catchment_redundancy_map.Rd

Shows, for each target polygon, roughly how many distinct providers' drive-time catchment areas reach it – 1 means that area has exactly one option within range, 0 means none do, and higher numbers mean more redundant coverage. This is the complement of a simple access map: access maps show whether a provider is reachable at all, this shows how much choice a reader at that location actually has.

Usage

mysterymaps_catchment_redundancy_map(
  catchments,
  polygons,
  provider_id_var,
  title = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  caption = NULL,
  grid_spacing_miles = 5,
  k = 6,
  zero_color = "#e0e0e0",
  na_color = "#ffffff",
  crs = 5070
)

Arguments

catchments

sf polygon layer, one row per provider catchment (single drive-time band; see Details).

polygons

sf polygon layer: the target areas to summarize onto (e.g. counties).

provider_id_var

character(1): column in catchments identifying the distinct provider.

title, subtitle, caption

Character labels. NULL omits.

grid_spacing_miles

numeric(1): sample grid spacing, in miles. Default 5. Smaller is more accurate and slower.

k

integer(1): target number of Jenks classes for the positive (1-or-more) redundancy counts, passed to mysterymaps_jenks_zero_scale(). Default 6.

zero_color, na_color

Colours for a measured-zero (no coverage at all) and an unmeasured polygon, respectively. Defaults match mysterymaps_jenks_zero_scale()'s own.

crs

Projection for display. Default EPSG:5070 (Albers Equal Area), appropriate for the contiguous United States.

Value

A ggplot object. The caller saves it; this function writes nothing.

Details

Redundancy is estimated with a sample grid rather than an exact polygon overlay, because an exact pairwise overlay across many overlapping catchments is expensive and the exact boundary of that overlay is not what the map needs – a representative per-polygon summary is. A regular point grid (grid_spacing_miles apart, in EPSG:5070 meters) is laid over the union of catchments' bounding box and polygons; each grid point counts the number of distinct provider_id_var values among the catchments containing it (0 if none); each target polygon's value is the median grid-point count among points falling inside it. Median, not mean, so one corner with much higher or lower redundancy than the rest of a large, irregularly-shaped polygon does not dominate its summary value.

A small polygon can be narrower than grid_spacing_miles and catch zero grid points at all – on Virginia's independent cities (Lexington, Fairfax City, Manassas, Manassas Park, Colonial Heights, Covington, Poquoson, Emporia, Bristol, Charlottesville; all under 20 square miles) this left 10 of 133 polygons with no sample at all, rendered as a blank gap in na.value even though they are not actually missing data. Any polygon the grid misses entirely is sampled once more directly, at sf::st_point_on_surface() (guaranteed to land inside the polygon, unlike a bounding-box centroid, which can fall outside an irregular shape).

A redundancy count is classified, not coloured continuously: 0 – nothing covers this area at all – is as categorically different from 1 as 1 is different from 5, and a continuous scale_fill_viridis_c() (the original implementation) puts 0 at the dark end of the same gradient as every low-but-nonzero value, where it reads as merely "low redundancy" rather than the "no option at all" finding it actually is. mysterymaps_jenks_zero_scale() with digits = NULL gives whole-number legend labels appropriate to a count and puts 0 in its own class, so it replaces the old scale_fill_viridis_c() plus a hand-written integer-breaks helper.

catchments must contain exactly one row per (provider, band) you want counted. If catchments holds multiple drive-time bands per provider, filter to a single band before calling this function – passing all bands at once would double-count the same provider at a point reachable within more than one of their bands.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive()
counties <- sf::st_sf(
  geometry = sf::st_sfc(lapply(1:2, function(i) {
    x <- -100 + i
    sf::st_polygon(list(cbind(c(x, x + 1, x + 1, x, x), c(40, 40, 41, 41, 40))))
  }), crs = 4326)
)
# county 1 is covered by provider A only, county 2 by both A and B
catch_a <- sf::st_sf(provider = "A", geometry = sf::st_sfc(
  sf::st_polygon(list(cbind(c(-99, -97, -97, -99, -99), c(40, 40, 42, 42, 40)))),
  crs = 4326))
catch_b <- sf::st_sf(provider = "B", geometry = sf::st_sfc(
  sf::st_polygon(list(cbind(c(-98, -97, -97, -98, -98), c(40, 40, 41, 41, 40)))),
  crs = 4326))
mysterymaps_catchment_redundancy_map(
  rbind(catch_a, catch_b), counties, provider_id_var = "provider",
  grid_spacing_miles = 10)
}
